speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) in respect of a woman who is older than 40 years old, why is she required to have attempted assisted reproduction or intra-uterine insemination (IUI) procedures before age 40 to be eligible for Government co-funded Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) procedures; and (b) whether this requirement can be removed as women are marrying later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The Assisted Reproduction Technology (ART) co-funding scheme was introduced to support couples who face difficulty in conceiving naturally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The age criterion of 40 years old is set based on current clinical evidence which shows that the chance of conception for a woman who undergoes ART treatment decreases with age, with significantly lower success rate after 40.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The ART co-funding is therefore directed towards those who attempted their first assisted reproduction procedure before age 40.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Couples are encouraged to start their families early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Those with difficulty conceiving should also consider fertility or ART treatment early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to monitor the clinical evidence and update the eligibility criteria where appropriate.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First, for those who marry late, for example, if they marry at age 40, it is impossible to meet the requirement to carry out IUI before age 40.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is, residents tell me that they are normally encouraged to do IUI first, and then IVF, as IUI is less invasive but the success rate is much lower.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The third question is, can the Ministry encourage people to go straight for IVF for those age 35 and above, so as not to waste time and money?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I was told the process to make appointment could take a few months to a year.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There is one more question, can Ministry remove the requirement of having to go through at least two rounds of IUI before going for IVF?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Give couples an option to go for IVF directly and this can save the women time and inconvenience.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I will take the question about the requirement for couples to go through either IUI or AR before age 40, before they are eligible for co-funding for AR procedure in our public AR centres at age 40 or above.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, let me say that we recognise that more couples are getting married later and they do have parenthood aspirations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But unfortunately, even though there have been improvements in technology as well as better understanding of treatment needs, embryo culture and so on, the empirical evidence still shows that the success rate is very much linked to when the procedures are performed on the women.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, when we put the age criterion of 40 years, as I have said, we recognise that people are getting married later, and we do not want to put too low a cut-off age.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The experts also feel that age 40 is reasonable, given the empirical evidence before them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, this age criterion, together with the requirement that couples need to have already tried AR or IUI before age 40 to qualify for this co-funding, really, the intent is to balance the need to support and encourage couples to receive AR procedures early for higher chance of success and at the same time, also, to support the needs of older couples who want to try for a child.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is a balanced approach, taking into account the scientific data and the social trends as well as the developments to date.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to monitor the clinical evidence and where appropriate, we will update the eligibility criteria.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the IUI co-funding, we only introduced this in January 2020.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It was done to enhance our support for couples who have difficulties conceiving naturally.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: IUI, as the Member has rightly pointed out, is a less invasive procedure.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, depending on the assessment of the doctors, they will be advised whether they can go through IUI with co-funding up to three cycles before going to IVF, which is up to six cycles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I do not have the success rates for IUI here, but I can give the information to the Member later.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There was also a question of couples marrying beyond age 40 and then, they are not eligible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is only for the Government co-funding that they will not be eligible for.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The reason is because we need also to be mindful of the effectiveness of such financial support extended through Government co-funding.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This has to be based objectively on the empirical evidence before us.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I agree with the Senior Minister of State that we need to be very careful with the funding.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: But I have one question, my second question earlier, for those who are aged 35 and above, instead of asking them to go through IUI, can we let them have an option to go for IVF?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Many of them say that the success rate for IUI is very low and it is a waste of their time as their biological clock is not with them.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Maybe the Ministry can consider letting them choose, give them an option to go for IVF straightaway.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, my understanding is whether to go IUI before going to IVF really depends on the doctors' assessment.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I will have to stand corrected, but I do not think there is a policy that couples definitely have to go through IUI before IVF.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But as the Member has also pointed out and also according to my understanding, IUI is less invasive, so it may be something that doctors advise them to try before going through AR procedures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have also said, even for AR, for women younger than age 30, where the success rate is highest, it is actually about 24%.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I agree with the Senior Minister of State that our policies should be based on science.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But science also tells us that stress faced is a key factor in determining whether an IVF is successful.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think a lot of the couples are very stressed because of the finances involved in an IVF cycle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If MOH can then provide the subsidies, reduce the stress, then, maybe we will have a higher percentage of success for IVF cycles for those age 40 and above.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, such policies have to be objectively determined based on the empirical evidence.
